title: Three Days and One Short Bowl
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：sugar　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sugar 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the cook ① added the sugar that no guest in the canteen would have described, and he said the adding was the whole of the day. The ② sugar, meaning the crystal itself and not the bowl, ran three days and stayed undescribed in the book; sugar, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ spoonful of sugar in that canteen had the same short bowl beside it, and the ④ sugar at the far table, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Sugar, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the cook said the describing is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the sugar was the whole of the matter, meaning the sweetness and not the crystal. The ⑥ sugar, meaning the sweetness and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; sugar, he said, is either something you add or the only word that means both crystal and a sweetness. He said the sweetness is the part they remember.

By 1983 the ⑦ sugar had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short bowl. The ⑧ sugar of the whole thing, the cook wrote in September, was one canteen and three days of describing; sugar, he said, is either the portion at the far table or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ sugar I remember is the sugar described in the menu, which closed in 1985 and is still described as the quietest in the canteen. ⑩ Sugar, my mother said in 1987, is the only thing that improves by being described; all sugar, she said, is a sweetness that has agreed to look like crystal. She said the sweetness was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 糖（指食堂里每一勺旁边的那一勺）
B. n. 糖（指那勺糖本身，与小小的碗相对）
C. 固定搭配：add the sugar 加这一勺糖
D. n. 糖（指留给孩子们分着吃的那一份）
E. n. 糖之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的糖之事）
F. n. 糖（指菜单里写到、被描述的那一勺）
G. n. 糖、甜头（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 甜头（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: added the sugar that no guest in the canteen would have described
The sugar, meaning the crystal itself and not the bowl

the sugar at the far table
the sugar was the whole of the matter
the sugar had become a line in a menu
The sugar of the whole thing

answers.why: add the sugar 意为“加这一勺糖”，1978 年那位厨子把食堂里没有一位客人肯描述的一勺糖做了一遍。
sugar 意为“糖”，指那勺糖本身而不是小小的碗，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被描述。
sugar 意为“糖”，指食堂里每一勺旁边的那一勺，每一勺旁边都有同一只小小的碗。
sugar 意为“糖”，指最远那张桌角的留给孩子们分着吃的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
sugar 意为“糖、甜头”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这勺甜头就是那件事的全部。
sugar 意为“甜头”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那勺糖，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
sugar 意为“糖”，指菜单里写到、被描述的那一勺，到 1983 年这一勺成了菜单里的一行。
sugar 意为“糖之事”，厨子九月写道，整件事的糖之事是一处食堂和三个日子的描述。
sugar 意为“糖”，我记得的是菜单里描述过的那一勺，1985 年开完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一勺。
sugar 为抽象总称，母亲 1987 年说，糖是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的糖。
